problem: General-purpose mapless neural agents (CNN+RNN encoders trained with large-scale model-free RL) nearly solve PointGoal navigation but fail at ObjectGoal navigation. The best such result was about 6% success, and large-scale training gives 94% success on training scenes but only 8% on validation.
motivation: The authors trace the ObjectNav failure to overfitting. Agents memorize training layouts and learn shortest paths to nearby goal objects instead of learning to explore. This behavior is encouraged by the task metric (SPL penalizes exploration), enabled by powerful observation encoders, and made possible by the small, finite set of training environment configurations. If the number of distinct training layouts can be expanded, general-purpose models might learn to explore and generalize.
key_idea: Augment ObjectNav training by inserting 3D scans of household objects at arbitrary scene locations and using them as goals ('treasure hunt'). This greatly expands the set of training layouts, so agents cannot memorize and must learn to explore.
insight: ObjectNav generalization with end-to-end RL is limited mainly by memorization of a finite set of scenes, not by model capacity: train success is 94% while val success is 8%. Breaking the fixed mapping between scene and goal location with synthetic object insertion forces exploratory behavior. The abstract also argues that optimizing the task metric directly (SPL) works against exploration. The per-component contribution of THDA versus the paper's 'other proposed changes' cannot be stated from the abstract alone.
method: Overfitting analysis: shows that large-scale RL on ObjectNav reaches 94% train vs 8% val success, and attributes this to layout memorization enabled by strong encoders, a finite set of environments, and an exploration-penalizing metric.

Treasure Hunt Data Augmentation (THDA): inserts 3D-scanned household objects at arbitrary locations in training scenes and uses them as ObjectNav goal targets, multiplying the number of training layouts and goal configurations.

General-purpose agent: mapless neural policy built from task-agnostic components (CNN observation encoder + RNN), trained with large-scale model-free RL (DD-PPO-style, per the PointNav prior work it builds on).
Other proposed changes (not detailed in abstract): additional training modifications combined with THDA to counter the exploration-penalizing objective and overfitting.

setting.backbone: CNN encoder + RNN policy trained from scratch with large-scale model-free RL (exact architecture not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: Habitat ObjectNav training scenes (Matterport3D) augmented with inserted 3D scans of household objects as extra goals (THDA); scale not given in abstract
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (+ GPS/compass per standard Habitat ObjectNav setting; not stated in abstract)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level Habitat ObjectNav actions (exact set not stated in abstract)

numbers_note: abstract only. The abstract states results on the Habitat ObjectGoal Navigation benchmark (likely MP3D, Habitat Challenge): SR rises from 14% to 27% and SPL from 7.5 to 11.1. It also reports 94% train vs 8% val success for plain large-scale training. Split and eval details are not available.
results: On the Habitat ObjectGoal Navigation benchmark, THDA combined with the paper's other changes raises the state of the art from 14% to 27% success rate (+90% relative). SPL rises from 7.5 to 11.1 (+48% relative). This also far exceeds the prior best general-purpose-model result of about 6% success.
limitations: Absolute performance remains low (27% SR, 11.1 SPL), so ObjectNav is far from solved with general-purpose models.
Inserted objects are 3D scans placed at arbitrary locations, which may not respect realistic object-scene semantics or context.
Evaluation is simulation-only on Habitat/MP3D; no real-robot validation is mentioned in the abstract.
compares_to: Habitat ObjectNav Challenge 2020 entries (prior SOTA 14% SR)
